newsitem.title: USA: Lebed says he wants an inauguration like Clinton's.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says he wants an inauguration like Clinton's.

text.p: Alexander Lebed, who flaunts his ambition to take over the presidency of Russia, watched President Bill Clinton's inauguration on Monday and said he hoped for a similar ceremony for himself one day.
The tough-talking retired general, who does little to disguise his contempt for Russian's ailing leader, Boris Yeltsin, attended the event as a guest of Republican Sen. Bill Roth of Delaware.

Asked whether he saw himself taking part in a similar ceremony one day, an unsmiling Lebed told Reuters television: "Well, I hope I will and I am going to learn how to do it. I am going to learn how to correctly organise an inauguration."

Lebed's announcement last week in Moscow that Clinton had invited him to attend the ceremony puzzled the White House, which does not generally invite foreign dignitaries to an inauguration and which has made support for Yeltsin a cornerstone of its Russia policy. It eventually emerged he had been invited by Roth as one of the guests he could invite in his capacity as a congressman.

Roth, chairman of the North Atlantic Assembly, NATO's parliamentary forum, met Lebed in his office before the ceremony. Lebed opposes NATO expansion into East European countries that were previously members of the Soviet bloc but Roth strongly favours the policy.

"Our discussions were frank and to the point. I was pleased at General Lebed's flexibility on NATO enlargement and look forward to continuing discussions with him on the subject," Roth said in a statement.

Lebed, who arrived in Washington on Sunday, was due to visit Wilmington, Delaware, and New York before leaving for home on Thursday. He was accompanied at the inaugural ceremonies at the Capitol by his wife, who wore a long mink coat against the midwinter cold.
